inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,504 logical lines. This informal historical-computational survey follows the passage from empirical prime tables and prime-density heuristics through the zeta function, Euler products, explicit formulas, and RH-equivalent error terms; it then separates evaluation, critical-zero location, and completeness certification, compares Euler-Maclaurin, Gram, Riemann-Siegel, Turing, and Odlyzko-Schoenhage methods, and traces applications to exact prime counts, explicit bounds, false inequalities, Mertens, Goldbach, L-functions, pair correlation, and random matrices. The prose is coherent, but displayed formulas should be checked against the retained PDF before formula-level training use.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and prime-counting motivation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces pi(x), the sum-to-integral heuristic behind Li(x), the PNT, explicit prime bounds, and the RH-conditional accuracy scale.

sections_inspected.label: Zeta, continuation, symmetry, and RH foundations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the complex-analytic turn, elementary PNT contrast, analytic continuation, functional equation, xi-factorization, zero symmetries, and the RH statement.

sections_inspected.label: Euler products, explicit formulas, and prime-error viewpoints
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects unique factorization to the Euler product, zeros to prime-counting formulas, weighted Chebyshev functions to the logarithmic derivative, zero-free regions to error terms, and Möbius inversion to R(x).

sections_inspected.label: Transition to computational certification
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recalls the rediscovery of Riemann's approximate formulas and separates zeta evaluation, critical-zero location, and proof that all zeros up to a height were found.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Euler-Maclaurin formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents a sum-integral correction expansion, explicit remainder control, and its linear-in-height computational limitation.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Gram test
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Turns the critical-line zeta function into a real Hardy Z-function and uses Gram-point signs to bracket critical zeros, including failure and recovery cases.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Total number of zeros up to a given height
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops zero-counting through N(T), theta(T), and S(T), diagnoses Backlund's limitations, and records results on the proportion of critical zeros.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Riemann-Siegel formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the short oscillatory main sum from a contour representation and isolates the remainder bound needed for certified evaluation.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Turing's method
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains how averaging the discrepancy between observed and total zero counts certifies that no zeros were missed.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Odlyzko-Schoenhage method
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recasts many Dirichlet-polynomial evaluations as rational-function evaluation at roots of unity and compares algorithmic complexity.

sections_inspected.label: 7. A brief history of non-trivial zeros calculations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Tracks the scale and provenance of zero computations and notes reproducibility/publication limitations.

sections_inspected.label: 8. Applications
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses finite zero data and explicit formulas for exact pi(x), explicit inequalities, sign changes, the Mertens counterexample mechanism, and the ternary Goldbach proof pipeline.

sections_inspected.label: 9.1. Complex analytic number theory
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Abstracts Riemann's method into the Dirichlet-series, Perron-integral, contour-shift reflex for irregular arithmetic functions.

sections_inspected.label: 9.2. The Zeta Zoo
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers the zeta template to Dirichlet and Dedekind L-functions and lists the Selberg-class-style structural properties.

sections_inspected.label: 9.3. Correlation of pairs of non-trivial zeros
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Normalizes zero spacing, states pair correlation, and interprets its small-gap suppression as zero repulsion and evidence for simplicity.

sections_inspected.label: 9.4. Random matrix theory
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates zero statistics to Hermitian spectra, uses the dictionary to conjecture zeta moments, and contrasts numerical evidence with function-field theorems.

sections_inspected.label: 10. Words of warning
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains why iterated-log asymptotics can masquerade as bounded behavior and make unsupported numerical conjecture hazardous.

sections_inspected.label: Further reading, acknowledgements, and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Accounts for source recommendations, acknowledgements, bibliography, page furniture, and author metadata.

accepted_units.title: Prime tables suggest a local probability whose cumulative form is an integral
accepted_units.why_material: Gauss's empirical thinning heuristic replaces a count by a sum of local densities and then by Li(x), making the recurring sum-to-integral move explicit before stating the PNT scale.
accepted_units.context_note: The probability language is heuristic; the asymptotic theorem is introduced later in the survey.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; the definitions of pi(x) and Li(x) should be checked against the PDF for exact typesetting.

accepted_units.title: RH matters because it would turn Li(x) into a uniformly sharp prime-counting surrogate
accepted_units.why_material: The span distinguishes the PNT's first-order asymptotic from explicit two-sided estimates and the much sharper RH-conditional error, while noting that unavoidable prime irregularity rules out an even smaller proposed scale.
accepted_units.context_note: The explicit inequality is reported from the literature, not proved in this survey.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and O-terms are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Complexifying the zeta variable transformed the prime-number problem
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts Euler's real-variable series with Riemann's analytic-function viewpoint and explains how later complex-function foundations converted the conceptual leap into the PNT proof tradition.
accepted_units.context_note: This is historical synthesis rather than a proof of the PNT.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low.

accepted_units.title: An elementary PNT proof reproduces the theorem without reproducing Riemann's structural leverage
accepted_units.why_material: Selberg's symmetry identity supports an elementary proof and extension to arithmetic progressions, but the survey records that hopes for broader new insight from avoiding complex analysis were not realized.
accepted_units.context_note: The identity is displayed without a full derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extracted symmetry formula needs PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Continuation and completion expose the zeta function's reflection symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Two continuation devices lead to the meromorphic zeta function and its functional equation; multiplying by the polar factors produces the entire xi-function whose zeros are precisely the nontrivial zeta zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The continuation formulas are illustrative and the full-plane continuation is stated rather than proved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula dependence; gamma and exponent placement should be verified.

accepted_units.title: Hadamard factorization and the functional equation organize zeros into fourfold symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: The completed-function product turns zeros into factors, while functional-equation and conjugation symmetries reduce computation to one region and identify the critical line and finite-height RH certification target.
accepted_units.context_note: The survey reports Riemann's hypothesis and historical wording; it does not establish RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Hadamard product and theta transformation are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Euler products encode primes while explicit formulas reconstruct their count from zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Unique factorization becomes an Euler product, its singularity implies infinitely many primes, and Riemann's explicit formula expresses pi(x) as a smooth R(x) term corrected by every nontrivial zero; the table illustrates why R(x) improves Li(x).
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed explicit formula is presented informally and its summation convention is not developed here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive; the table is useful but not essential.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic weights make the prime-zero correspondence analytically natural
accepted_units.why_material: The von Mangoldt weight arises from logarithmically differentiating the Euler product, simplifies the explicit formula for psi(x), and makes the rightmost zero's real part control the prime-counting error, yielding an RH-equivalent error exponent.
accepted_units.context_note: The source warns implicitly that summing zero contributions requires truncation because the naive absolute sum diverges.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact sums, truncations, and logarithmic powers require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Moving a zero-free boundary left improves prime errors, but known regions remain far from a power saving
accepted_units.why_material: Von Koch's equivalence makes the critical-line location an error exponent, while explicit zero-free regions show how partial exclusion of zeros yields weaker PNT errors and expose the stubborn gap to any fixed x-to-a-power improvement.
accepted_units.context_note: The reported region and constants are historical best-known values as of the survey.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The zero-free-region denominator is degraded and must be checked.

accepted_units.title: Replacing prime probability by the average of Lambda leads naturally to psi, Pi, and R
accepted_units.why_material: The average-one heuristic for the von Mangoldt function unifies equivalent PNT forms; counting prime powers and applying Möbius inversion then produces R(x) as a principled refinement of Li(x).
accepted_units.context_note: The passage is explicitly heuristic until connected to the cited exact identities.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Pi(x) and Möbius-inversion formulas require layout verification.

accepted_units.title: Numerical RH verification separates evaluation, localization, and completeness
accepted_units.why_material: The rediscovery of Riemann's approximate formulas leads to a three-stage certification architecture: compute zeta accurately, locate critical-line zeros, and independently count all strip zeros up to the height so agreement has evidential force.
accepted_units.context_note: Counts at finite height are evidence and certification only for that range, never a proof of global RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low.

accepted_units.title: Euler-Maclaurin makes zeta computable with a certified but linearly growing cost
accepted_units.why_material: A finite Dirichlet sum plus Bernoulli corrections and a controlled remainder gives prescribed-precision evaluation; the number of required terms grows linearly with the imaginary part, explaining why the simple method loses at height.
accepted_units.context_note: The exact expansion is readable but extracted Bernoulli notation is crowded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; verify the series, remainder inequality, and indices against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The Hardy Z-function turns critical zeros into real sign changes sampled at Gram points
accepted_units.why_material: Phase rotation makes critical-line zeta real, asymptotic phase monotonicity defines Gram points, and endpoint signs bracket zeros; empty intervals paired with neighboring double intervals show how the rule can fail locally without defeating computation.
accepted_units.context_note: A sign change proves an odd number of roots in the interval, while absence of a sign change alone does not prove no root.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Definitions of Z(t), theta(t), and its asymptotic are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Argument variation counts all strip zeros but pointwise control of S(T) is fragile
accepted_units.why_material: N(T) and the argument term S(T) provide a total-zero count to compare with located critical zeros; Backlund's nearest-integer shortcut is obstructed by contour nonvanishing and unbounded S(T), and multiple zeros expose a separate failure mode.
accepted_units.context_note: Random-matrix evidence for simplicity is reported as conjectural and numerical, not as certification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The log-xi identity, contour definition, and constants require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Positive proportions quantify progress without collapsing into full RH
accepted_units.why_material: The historical chain from infinitely many critical zeros to a positive fraction and then successively improved constants provides a calibrated intermediate signal distinct from proving every zero critical.
accepted_units.context_note: Values are reported as of 2018 and should not be treated as current without external verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; numerical constants should be checked.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel replaces a length-t sum by a square-root-length oscillatory sum plus a controlled remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Two evaluations of a contour integral produce the short cosine sum for Z(t); saddle-point analysis expands the remainder, and an explicit bound is what upgrades fast approximation into certified computation.
accepted_units.context_note: The source sketches the derivation and reports a particular historical bound rather than proving all coefficients.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; contour orientation, cutoff, coefficients, and remainder exponents need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Turing averages the counting discrepancy so any missed zeros create an impossible persistent bias
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing the unknown total count by the observed critical-zero count shifts S(t) downward by the number missed; an integral bound on S prevents that shift from persisting and yields a finite extra-height buffer for certification.
accepted_units.context_note: The method certifies completeness only under its numerical and analytic error controls.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integral inequality and constants require formula verification.

accepted_units.title: A Fourier transform makes many nearby zeta evaluations cheaper than isolated evaluations
accepted_units.why_material: Odlyzko-Schoenhage maps an evenly sampled Dirichlet polynomial to rational-function values at roots of unity, so FFT-style batching changes the asymptotic cost of large zero-verification runs without improving a single evaluation.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is summarized and its implementation details are not given.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The two transformed sums and complexity parameters are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Zero-verification records scale through algorithms and distributed computation but still require reproducible evidence
accepted_units.why_material: The chronological table and prose connect methodological advances to orders-of-magnitude growth and explicitly flag that two enormous computations were neither independently repeated nor published in a mathematical journal.
accepted_units.context_note: A reported computation is not elevated to formal or independently replicated evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The record table is required for exact counts and dates.

accepted_units.title: Explicit formulas trade exhaustive prime enumeration for a finite certified zero input
accepted_units.why_material: The evolution from combinatorial prime counting to Platt's unconditional explicit-formula computation shows how sufficiently accurate, complete critical-zero data can certify an exact pi(x) value far beyond direct enumeration.
accepted_units.context_note: The survey gives the result and data requirements, not the complete interval-arithmetic proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact numerical thresholds and the displayed pi value should be checked.

accepted_units.title: Partial RH converts a verified zero range into explicit prime inequalities on a bounded x-range
accepted_units.why_material: The span traces explicit bounds for pi, theta, and the nth prime to finite-height zero verification and states a direct relation between an RH height and the x-range on which an RH-strength inequality follows.
accepted_units.context_note: The transfer has explicit range conditions; it does not extend finite verification to all x.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Constants, counts, and the height-to-x inequality require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: A tiny zero-driven oscillation can overturn an overwhelmingly persistent prime-counting bias
accepted_units.why_material: The explicit formula explains why pi(x)-Li(x) must oscillate despite vast initial evidence, while accurately known zeros plus Lehman's bounds locate a region of reversed inequality and logarithmic density quantifies the remaining bias.
accepted_units.context_note: The density statement is conditional on additional plausible conjectures, as the source says.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The explicit formula, huge bounds, and density value are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: The Mertens conjecture failed when an explicit zero sum was phase-aligned by Diophantine optimization
accepted_units.why_material: The reciprocal-zeta representation gives RH and PNT equivalences for M(x), a random-walk heuristic already warns against the square-root bound, and the disproof combines a truncated zero formula, certified roots and simplicity, simultaneous phase alignment, and LLL.
accepted_units.context_note: The derivation of the truncated formula assumes RH and simple zeros, while the cited disproof conclusion is unconditional through its full rigorous argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; integral identities, limsup bounds, and phase terms need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Ternary Goldbach closes by combining arc estimates with certified Dirichlet-L zero ranges
accepted_units.why_material: The progression from GRH-conditional asymptotics through explicit bounds to Helfgott's unconditional proof shows computation serving as a bounded verification component inside a proof whose large range is handled analytically.
accepted_units.context_note: Binary Goldbach remains distinct and is reported only as numerically verified to a finite bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Huge numerical cutoffs and the q-dependent height require verification.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet series regularize erratic arithmetic data and contour shifting returns information to sums
accepted_units.why_material: The source abstracts a reusable Riemann reflex: encode an arithmetic function in a Dirichlet series, recover its summatory function by Perron's integral, shift the contour using continuation, and if necessary replace the function by a better-behaved proxy before transferring conclusions back.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a methodological sketch with convergence hypotheses, not a general theorem as stated.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Perron integral and convergence line are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: The zeta template generalizes through a package of series, growth, continuation, reflection, and Euler factors
accepted_units.why_material: Dirichlet and Dedekind examples show how prime-distribution questions migrate to L-functions; the five listed Selberg-style properties separate the reusable architecture from the Riemann zeta function's particular coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: The list is an informal characterization and should not be mistaken for a complete definition of every zeta-like function.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The coefficient-growth and product formulas should be checked.

accepted_units.title: Rescaling zeros to unit mean spacing reveals repulsion through pair correlation
accepted_units.why_material: The N(T) asymptotic motivates unfolding the ordinates, Montgomery's pair statistic predicts suppressed near-collisions, and both a smooth theorem and Odlyzko's data connect the statistic to zero simplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: The full pair-correlation formula is conjectural and the discussion assumes RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The unfolding and limiting integral require exact formula verification; the later figure supports the numerical comparison.

accepted_units.title: Random Hermitian spectra supply a statistical model for zeta zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Dyson's recognition transfers Montgomery's zero-spacing law to a random-matrix ensemble, providing a model that generates otherwise inaccessible conjectures and makes high-height numerical checks scientifically important.
accepted_units.context_note: Similarity of statistics is not a proof that a corresponding operator or universal dictionary exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low.

accepted_units.title: Random matrices predict the full hierarchy of zeta moments and are calibrated by known cases
accepted_units.why_material: Known first and second moments establish anchors, matrix size near log(T/2pi) supplies the translation, and Keating-Snaith values extend the coefficient pattern to all moments while analytic special cases and high-zero computations test the dictionary.
accepted_units.context_note: The general moment formula and the random-matrix dictionary remain conjectural; the figure is numerical evidence only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Essential formula/figure dependency for the moment normalization, f(k), and Odlyzko spacing plot.

accepted_units.title: Function fields turn parts of the random-matrix dictionary into theorems
accepted_units.why_material: A structurally related setting where RH is known lets Katz-Sarnak prove random-matrix predictions, offering exact analogue evidence without transferring those proofs automatically to number fields.
accepted_units.context_note: The survey states the analogy broadly and does not specify the individual function-field theorems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low.

accepted_units.title: Iterated logarithms can make divergent behavior look bounded on every feasible computation
accepted_units.why_material: The warning explains a concrete mechanism behind false computational conjectures: asymptotically unbounded functions such as iterated logarithms can remain visually flat, so numerics need theoretical or heuristic support.
accepted_units.context_note: Mertens is an example of the danger, not evidence that every numerically motivated conjecture fails.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Explicit formulas make zeros both explanatory variables and computational inputs for primes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Euler products encode primes into zeta, explicit formulas decode prime statistics from zeros, zero-free geometry controls asymptotic error, and finite certified zero sets support exact computations or localized sign reversals.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Finite zero data transfers only to bounded numerical claims, and the survey's formulas require primary-source verification before exact reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Reliable RH computation is a pipeline, not a list of apparent critical zeros
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Fast, error-controlled zeta evaluation produces candidates; real sign methods locate critical zeros; independent zero counts and Turing averaging certify completeness; batching improves scale while provenance and replication preserve evidential quality.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The pipeline verifies only a finite height and does not establish global RH or zero simplicity beyond the certified inputs.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Counterexample computation succeeds when analytic structure reduces search to controlled phases
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For pi-Li and Mertens, explicit zero expansions identify the oscillatory coordinates, certified truncation bounds control omitted terms, and numerical or lattice methods align enough phases to force a rigorous sign or magnitude reversal.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The Mertens mechanism uses additional assumptions in its explanatory derivation, and the two counterexamples have different final rigor pathways.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The zeta reflex transfers one representation architecture across arithmetic families
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Arithmetic data are encoded by Dirichlet series and Euler factors, continuation enables contour movement, functional equations organize symmetry, and finite L-zero certification can then become an input to explicit additive-number-theory proofs.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Sharing this architecture does not make all zeta or L-functions interchangeable, and the survey gives only broad family-level conditions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Unfolded zero statistics support a random-matrix conjecture engine with an analogue check
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After normalizing local density, zeta zeros match random Hermitian eigenvalue statistics; the dictionary predicts spacing and moment laws, high-zero computations calibrate them, and function fields prove related predictions in a tractable analogue.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Statistical agreement and function-field theorems do not prove the number-field dictionary or RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Good numerical heuristics combine structural derivation with explicit falsification risk
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Gauss's and Riemann's heuristics are anchored in local densities, weighted averages, and inversion identities, whereas raw bounded-looking data can conceal iterated-log divergence; conceptual support changes what numerical persistence should mean.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Structural motivation still does not turn a heuristic into proof.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,077 logical lines. Soundararajan's paper builds a resonance method for extreme values by correlating a tunable Dirichlet polynomial with zeta or a family of central L-values, reducing existence to a ratio of quadratic forms. It optimizes a sparse multiplicative resonator for zeta, proves frequency bounds with second and fourth moments, and then transfers the architecture to quadratic characters and holomorphic cusp forms by replacing time orthogonality with character-square and Petersson orthogonality. The extracted prose and proof architecture are coherent; exact formulas, constants, and indices remain PDF-dependent.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Large values of zeta: proof of Theorem 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Diagonalizes smoothed resonator moments, optimizes multiplicative coefficients from below and above, and proves both existence and frequency of large zeta values.

accepted_units.title: A correlated Dirichlet polynomial turns extreme zeta values into quadratic-form optimization
accepted_units.why_material: After stating the large-value and frequency targets, the source defines smoothed unweighted and zeta-weighted moments of a resonator R(t); their ratio lower-bounds the maximum, and diagonal evaluation makes both moments quadratic forms in tunable coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: Gaussian and maximum-size predictions in the introduction are heuristic comparisons; Theorem 1 proves the stated lower bounds only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; theorem ranges, moment definitions, and normalizations require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The same resonator can force both large and small quadratic-character central values
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 and its context frame the first family transfer: central values over fundamental discriminants admit opposite exponential extremes even amid nonvanishing and positivity questions.
accepted_units.context_note: Chowla positivity is reported as a conjecture; small nonzero values do not refute it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants, discriminant range, and exponential scale are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Functional-equation parity gates which cusp-form family can exhibit central extremes
accepted_units.why_material: The source defines the Hecke family and L-function, uses the functional-equation sign to exclude weights with forced central zero, states large and small value results for the even-sign family, and identifies further contexts where resonance transfers.
accepted_units.context_note: Theorem 3 is deliberately not optimized, as the author states.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Fourier normalization, parity, and theorem constants need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Fourier decay makes the resonator moments diagonal and exposes the correlation ratio
accepted_units.why_material: Compact smoothing turns distinct Dirichlet frequencies into rapidly decaying off-diagonal Fourier terms; the two evaluated moments reduce the zeta maximum to a ratio involving r(m)r(mk) over the coefficient energy.
accepted_units.context_note: The reduction requires the resonator length N to remain below a power of T.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; Fourier transforms, diagonal conditions, error terms, and the final ratio must be checked.

accepted_units.title: A sparse prime-supported multiplicative weight aligns the numerator while controlling mass
accepted_units.why_material: The lower-bound proof chooses squarefree multiplicative coefficients concentrated on an intermediate prime window, factors the denominator into an Euler product, and uses Rankin's trick to show truncation tails are negligible while the numerator gains coherently.
accepted_units.context_note: Prime-number-theorem estimates are invoked for the final asymptotics rather than derived here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact prime window, L definition, Euler products, and alpha choice are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: A tailored multiplicative majorant proves the resonator scale is essentially optimal
accepted_units.why_material: The upper-bound proof introduces g(k), splits each product r(mk)r(m) by a weighted quadratic inequality, regroups by coefficient energy, and bounds both divisor-side factors through Euler products, matching the lower construction's main exponential scale.
accepted_units.context_note: This bounds the optimization problem of Theorem 2.1, not all possible methods for large zeta values.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition of g and resulting product estimates require formula verification.

accepted_units.title: Known zeta moments already force a nontrivial measure of moderately large values
accepted_units.why_material: The proof separates the portion of the second moment above a threshold and uses Cauchy-Schwarz with the fourth moment to lower-bound the measure of that portion, covering the initial V range without a specialized long resonator.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the moderate-value regime; the larger-V range uses a different resonator length and fourth-moment control.

inspection_summary: Inspected all 712 logical lines. Paris and Cang derive a generalized incomplete-gamma smoothing of the zeta Dirichlet series, bound its correction remainder, specialize to real exponential smoothing, and show that the simplicity of the cutoff forces a Gram-type O(t) main sum rather than a Riemann-Siegel O(sqrt(t)) one. Numerical experiments expose parameter tradeoffs and the failure of the proved remainder bound near optimal truncation; appendices recover a known special case and prove monotonicity facts used in the bound. The scan's prose is recoverable, but displayed mathematics is heavily OCR-corrupted and all exact formula use requires the original pages.

accepted_units.title: Smoothing removes cutoff discontinuities but its parameter dependence decides whether the cost is Gram- or Riemann-Siegel-type
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction compares O(t) Euler-Maclaurin/Gram evaluation with the square-root-length Riemann-Siegel sum, reviews smooth error-function cutoffs, and isolates the paper's finding that a simpler real smoothing forces the effective cutoff back to O(t).
accepted_units.context_note: The cost comparison concerns the number of main-sum terms and does not by itself compare every implementation cost or error constant.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high; formulas (1.1)-(1.4), cutoff definitions, and OCR-confused symbols require the original scan.

accepted_units.title: An incomplete-gamma Mellin transform generates a family of smoothed zeta expansions
accepted_units.why_material: Absolute convergence licenses exchanging the sum and contour integral; moving the path collects the zeta and pole terms, then the functional equation and gamma-pole residues produce finite corrections plus a remainder, with a free smoothing parameter containing a known formula as a special case.
accepted_units.context_note: Computational usefulness also requires the shifted zeta values in the coefficients to lie in a convergent-series region.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Essential original-page dependency: equations (2.1)-(2.8) are substantially OCR-damaged, though the prose derivation and restrictions are clear.

accepted_units.title: Gamma-ratio monotonicity converts the contour remainder into a computable incomplete-gamma bound
accepted_units.why_material: After reflecting zeta and recentering the contour, the proof bounds the integral with an even increasing gamma ratio, rescales it by a decreasing function, evaluates the tail as an incomplete gamma function, and obtains a numerical remainder bound whose coefficient growth diagnoses the useful truncation range.
accepted_units.context_note: The monotonicity inputs are deferred to Appendix B, and the table shows the coefficient ceasing to be order one rather than proving sharpness of the final remainder bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Essential scan verification for equations (3.1)-(3.8), gamma ratios, and Table 1.

accepted_units.title: Real exponential smoothing forces a length-t cutoff and a finite optimal correction series
accepted_units.why_material: Setting the incomplete-gamma parameter to one makes the main sum exponentially smoothed, but asymptotic decrease of the correction terms requires K greater than t/(2pi), hence a Gram-type cutoff; the free power p accelerates decay while lowering optimal truncation and attainable accuracy.
accepted_units.context_note: The positive-integer restriction on p is adopted for simplicity and is not mathematically necessary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high; expansion (4.2), term sequence, optimal M formula, and parameter inequalities need the scan.

accepted_units.title: Actual critical-line errors validate suboptimal truncation but expose a nonuniform remainder bound
accepted_units.why_material: A concrete critical-line specialization supplies a computable Z(t) expansion and analytic remainder bound; tables compare optimal and deliberately suboptimal truncations, showing high accuracy for modest M but rapid deterioration of the bound well before the formal least term.
accepted_units.context_note: The tables test selected t and parameters and do not prove global error behavior.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Essential: formulas (4.5)-(4.6) and Tables 2-4 must be read from the original pages because the OCR is poor.

accepted_units.title: Increasing cutoff scale buys accuracy, while increasing smoothing power can destroy it
accepted_units.why_material: The final numerical comparison separates two effects: larger K extends the effective main sum and improves attainable accuracy, whereas larger p sharpens exponential decay but shortens the asymptotic correction series enough to reduce total accuracy.
accepted_units.context_note: The conclusions are empirical for the displayed t, K, p, and capped truncation choices, although they match the preceding asymptotic analysis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Table 5 is essential and requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Changing the smoothing shape preserves the Gram cost unless the parameter scales with s
accepted_units.why_material: The conclusion compares exponential and complementary-error-function choices, explains why the Berry-Keating logarithmic cutoff remains square-root length, identifies a transition from order-one to s-dependent parameters as open, and attributes remainder-bound failure to crude loss of oscillation.
accepted_units.context_note: The possibility of enormous optimal-truncation accuracy is conditional on an unproved asymptotic character of the expansion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The complementary-error-function expansion and remainder bound are badly OCR-damaged; the comparison prose is clear.

accepted_units.title: Pole cancellation and analytic continuation recover the earlier two-sided incomplete-gamma formula
accepted_units.why_material: Specializing the free parameters cancels gamma poles against trivial zeta zeros, reflection transforms the residual contour into the companion smoothed sum, and analytic continuation extends the identity before the critical-line parameter choice recovers formula (1.4).
accepted_units.context_note: This appendix checks consistency of representations rather than introducing a new computational advantage.
